Finish the missing Scotty3D core geometry code in `/workspace`. The renderer,
path tracer, and editor scaffolding already exist; the unfinished work is in
transform composition and the half-edge mesh operations that the editor and
tests depend on. Build from `/workspace` with `node Maekfile.js -j4`.

Focus on these files:

`src/scene/transform.cpp`
Implement `Transform::local_to_world()` and `Transform::world_to_local()` by
composing transforms along the parent chain. Do not fall back to a full
`Mat4::inverse()` call for the world-to-local path.

`src/geometry/halfedge-local.cpp`
Finish the local editing operations: edge bisection, edge splitting, edge
flipping on general polygons, edge collapse with manifold checks, face
extrusion, and the position update that applies move/shrink to an extruded
face. These routines must preserve half-edge invariants, handle boundary
cases correctly, and keep interpolated data consistent on newly created
elements.

`src/geometry/halfedge-global.cpp`
Restore the Catmull-Clark subdivision helper that performs the actual
topological split, then finish face-orientation reversal, corner-normal
computation, and per-face UV generation.

Keep the existing method signatures and semantics intact. The harness probes
the named APIs directly, including `Transform::local_to_world`,
`Transform::world_to_local`, `Halfedge_Mesh::bisect_edge`,
`split_edge`, `flip_edge`, `collapse_edge`, `extrude_face`,
`extrude_positions`, `catmark_subdivide_helper`, `flip_orientation`,
`set_corner_normals`, and `set_corner_uvs_per_face`.

When new mesh elements are created, use `interpolate_data({src1, src2}, dst)`
so UVs, normals, and bone-weight data propagate through the edit operation.
